title: fix(app-shell): a refused Rename view shows the server's reason as the toast description
body:
Fixes #12417
Clause-②: no

## What this does

`handleRenameView` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` showed a refused Rename view as the translated `objectViewActions.renameFailed` title with no options, so the server's reason reached `console.error` alone. The `catch` now passes the door's sentence as the toast description, through the channel objectui#11583 gave the view saves and objectui#12398 (PR #12414) gave Delete view: `formatMetadataError(err)` from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, with the `whitespace-pre-line` class. The translated title stays. There is no second extraction and no parsing of the message text: the shape is PR #12414's, byte for byte apart from the key.

Clause-② measured: no published `@object-ui/*` export, prop, type member or language-pack key moves. The change is the body of one internal handler's `catch`.

## Tests

All at head `4dae5a9a5`.

- **Pin:** the objectui#11583 harness `ObjectView.viewWriteRefusal-11583.test.tsx` turns its rename control into a pin. An `updateView` that throws a 403 refusal ("Renaming views requires the Manage Metadata permission") raises one `toast.error`; its title is `objectViewActions.renameFailed` and its description contains the door's sentence. The header names the rename row as this family's last silent view-write row.
- **Census:** the `handleRenameView` row of `writeRefusalCensus-11583.test.ts` keeps its kind and pin; its reason no longer reads "predates this census" and now says what the tree does (objectui#12417).
- **Ablation (one-time, not committed):** the fix was committed first. `ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack checkout) turned the anchor `toast.error(t('objectViewActions.renameFailed'), {` into `toast.error(t('objectViewActions.renameFailed')); ({`, so the options become a dead expression. On disk: anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, blob `673c6e67` to `038d527c`. Harness result: `Tests 1 failed | 13 passed (14)`; the only failure was the new pin, `expected 'undefined' to contain 'Renaming views requires the Manage Me…'`. Restored: blob equal to HEAD (`673c6e67`) and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- The harness plus the census, under the shared lock: 2 files, 21 tests, passed.
- Every `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.*` test plus the census: 65 files, 587 tests, passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after the `@object-ui/app-shell^...` closure build (exit 0).
- **NOT MEASURED: the full app-shell project.** Reason: `vitest run packages/app-shell/` under the shared lock was killed by its 1500 s timeout (exit 124) with no summary printed. Declared to CI.
- **Lint, narrowed to the 3 changed source files:** eslint `--no-inline-config --format json` read 3 files, 0 errors. The warnings on or near the changed lines are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` on the unchanged `(dataSource as any).updateView` lines. The narrowing excludes nothing: the root `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware parser options, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.
- **Gate battery, each exit 0:** `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`; also `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`. `check:spec-floors` exits 1 here with `no-artifact` (it wants a whole-workspace build); it is red on main too (objectui#12334). Recorded only.

## Acceptance notes

- With this change every view-write row of the objectui#11583 census says a refusal with the door's message.
- The published-half wrap PR #12414 noted for `deleteView` (the server's sentence only on `err.cause`) is a Delete-view matter; `updateView` was not probed for a similar wrap here. Out of this card's surface.
